old: plants that seed themselves, and every kind
why: Hebrew deshe esev mazria zera, 'plants yielding seed' (KJV 'herb yielding seed'); 'seed themselves' says self-sowing. 1:12 and 1:29 already say 'seed-bearing'. Hebrew from own knowledge.

old: Let them mark the seasons, the days, and the years
new: Let them be signs, and mark the seasons, the days, and the years
why: Hebrew vehayu le'otot ulemo'adim uleyamim veshanim: 'signs' (otot) is dropped (KJV 'let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years'). Hebrew from own knowledge. Mirror in the pilot.

old: Now he must not be allowed to reach out his hand and take from the tree of life too, and eat, and live forever.”
new: And now — what if he reaches out his hand and takes from the tree of life too, and eats, and lives forever —”
why: Hebrew ve'attah pen-yishlach yado... vachai le'olam breaks off unfinished and the narrative acts (KJV 'And now, lest he put forth his hand... and live for ever:'); the rendering completed it as a rule. Hebrew from own knowledge. Mirror in the pilot.

old: named him Seth — “because God has set
new: named him Seth — “because,” she said, “God has set
why: Hebrew ki shat-li elohim is Eve's speech (KJV 'For God, said she, hath appointed me'); as printed the quotation has no speaker. Hebrew from own knowledge.
Hebrew atsei-gopher is unidentified (KJV 'gopher wood'); 'cypress' is a scholarly guess printed as text. Same rule the edition applies to Nephilim and El Shaddai. Hebrew from own knowledge.
Hebrew zera vekatsir; KJV 'seedtime and harvest'. 'seedtime' is one English word; split, it misreads aloud.

old: And sons were born to Shem as well — the father of all the sons of Eber, the older brother of Japheth.
new: And sons were born to Shem as well — Shem, the older brother of Japheth, the father of all the sons of Eber.
why: As punctuated the appositive attaches to Eber. Hebrew avi kol-benei-ever achi yefet hagadol both describe Shem (KJV 'the father of all the children of Eber, the brother of Japheth the elder'). Hebrew from own knowledge.

old: And Abram gave him a tenth of everything.
new: And he gave him a tenth of everything.
why: Hebrew vayyitten-lo ma'aser mikkol has no named subject (KJV 'And he gave him tithes of all'); who paid whom is a known crux, and the text should leave it open. Hebrew from own knowledge.

old: “Have I really seen him here, and lived, after he saw me?”
new: “Have I really seen here the one who sees me?”
why: Received Hebrew hagam halom ra'iti acharei ro'i (KJV 'Have I also here looked after him that seeth me?'); 'and lived' comes from an emendation (elohim ra'iti va'echi), not the Masoretic text. Hebrew from own knowledge.

old: As I have kept faith with you, so you will keep faith with me
new: As I have shown you kindness, so you will show kindness to me
why: Hebrew kachesed asher-asiti immekha ta'aseh immadi (KJV 'according to the kindness that I have done unto thee'); the charter fixes hesed as 'kindness', and 19:19, 20:13, 24:12 use it. Hebrew from own knowledge.

old: God of the sky and God of the earth
new: God of heaven and God of the earth
why: Hebrew elohei hashamayim velohei ha'arets (KJV 'the God of heaven, and the God of the earth'): a divine title, not weather; cf. 'maker of heaven and earth' at 14:19, 14:22. Policy: shamayim as title or God's place = heaven. Hebrew from own knowledge.

old: The LORD, God of the sky, who took me
new: The LORD, God of heaven, who took me
why: Hebrew YHWH elohei hashamayim (24:7; KJV 'The LORD God of heaven'); same title as 24:3. Hebrew from own knowledge.

old: He settled alongside all his kin.
new: He settled at odds with all his kin.
why: Hebrew al-penei khol-echav nafal repeats the oracle of 16:12 (al-penei khol-echav yishkon), which the edition renders 'live at odds with all his brothers'; 'alongside' drops the hostility and the echo. Hebrew from own knowledge.

old: and this is the gate of the sky.
new: and this is the gate of heaven.
why: Hebrew sha'ar hashamayim, KJV 'this is the gate of heaven': God's dwelling, not the atmosphere, and the line must stay recognizable. Policy: shamayim as title or God's place = heaven. Hebrew from own knowledge.

old: that you have come after me so hot?
new: that you have come after me in hot pursuit?
why: Hebrew ki dalaqta acharai (KJV 'that thou hast so hotly pursued after me'); 'come after me so hot' is not idiomatic and stalls the line. Hebrew from own knowledge.
